answer: An agent market blunts sybil floods by forcing every new key to pre-commit a lotus of custody petals before the epoch's public randomness is known. After the beacon publishes its seed, a randomly chosen petal must open to a unique hardware or vault receipt, and a sparrow check — a short rerunnable hash of that receipt plus the seed — is what peers attest. Because the opening path is unknowable at commitment time, cloning one receipt across many keys fails the selected petal, and each extra identity demands a fresh slashable bond. Scripted farms then burn capital instead of minting weight.
